title: Kitchen Princess
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Orphan Najika, a gifted cook, enrolls at the elite Seika Academy hoping to find the boy who saved her from drowning and left her a spoon with the school's crest. Classmates look down on her, while two brothers, Sora and Daichi, recognize her talent, and a love triangle and family tragedies follow (Kodansha/Del Rey blurbs via AniList/MU; Manga Librarian).
life_message: Cooking with love for others can heal grief and win over people who first reject you.

content.note: Near-drowning in backstory (blurb review); car accident (MU).
A love interest dies in an accident midway (Manga Librarian); MU Car Accident, Death of Loved One/s; AniList Tragedy.
School-age love triangle (blurb, Manga Librarian); no sexual content noted.
Two-chapter eating-disorder storyline resolved quickly (Manga Librarian; MU Eating Disorder/s); grief of an orphan; bullying (AniList, Manga Librarian).
Class-based bullying; a bully becomes a best friend (Manga Librarian).

dominant: Kindness through cooking; overcoming class prejudice; grief and first love

frames.aligns: Works of mercy through feeding others; forgiveness of bullies.
frames.concerns: Death of a teen and eating disorder need discussion.

frames.aligns: Vocation and love of neighbor through food.
Simple service and mutual aid in feeding others.
Food offered with love as seva.

frames.concerns: Eating disorder storyline not safe-messaged (Manga Librarian).
Death used as plot device (Manga Librarian).
Ghost of the dead tag to verify.

frames.aligns: Langar-like feeding of others; equality across class.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Najika wins bullies over with kindness (Manga Librarian).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Elite academy rules versus personal quest.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Searching for a lost boy; brothers' family tensions (blurb).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Poor orphan rejected by elite students, then accepted (Manga Librarian).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Ordinary school drama; family memory central.

folkways.japan: An early-2000s Nakayoshi shoujo; elite academy rankings and quick treatment of mental health reflect that period's Japanese conventions (Manga Librarian).

delivery.evidence: Manga Librarian calls it 'a gentle read' with quick, tidy resolutions (to verify).
delivery.note: A bully becomes Najika's best friend, so rivals are given a way to change (Manga Librarian).

winners_losers: Najika's kindness wins people over; snobbery is shown as mistaken; one brother's death is described by a reviewer as a way to avoid choosing.
to_verify: Eating disorder storyline and its handling; MU Amnesia and AniList Ghost (spoiler) tags.
Manga Librarian suggests secondary readers and some upper elementary.
